Set up OpenCode

How to Use OpenCode 2 on Your First Project

Install OpenCode 2, open a small Git project and choose a model. For a first check without an API key, use a downloaded Ollama model, pass it a two-line file and compare its answer with the actual program output. Check Git status before moving to a project where edits matter.

  1. Install and check the version
  2. Choose a model provider
  3. Create a small test project
  4. Run and verify the first session
  5. Continue with your own repository

Install OpenCode 2 and check the version

Use the official installation options for your platform. On a system with npm, the V2 CLI package is @opencode/cli.

npm install -g @opencode/cli
opencode --version

If you already use OpenCode 1, keep a copy of the previous configuration and follow the migration instructions before installing. Both versions use the same command name by default. Confirm you are running V2 before copying the settings below.

Where will your model run?

Check OllamaConnect providerCompare options

Choose between local and hosted models

Use a local model if you can run it on your machine and want to avoid connecting a hosted account. The model must already be downloaded before an offline run. With a hosted model, use the provider credentials and check the provider’s usage or billing terms before sending prompts. Keep the first project free of private data in either case.

Check that OpenCode finds a local Ollama model

With Ollama running, use ollama list to confirm the exact installed tag. OpenCode discovers supported local models at its default Ollama address. From your project, open /models or run the following to find the exact ollama/ ID.

ollama list
opencode models --standalone

If the model is missing or the port differs, follow the OpenCode and Ollama connection check before running the tutorial.

Connect a hosted provider

Run opencode in the project, then open /connect. Pick the provider and follow its authentication prompts. Go to /models and select a model the project can use. Some accounts or plans restrict model access. Use the exact model ID shown by OpenCode if you switch to a terminal command.

For OpenCode’s hosted subscription, see Go usage limits and reset windows. The local test below uses Ollama.

Create a scratch project with a result you can verify

Create a new directory and run git init. Save this as total.py.

items = [2, 3]
print(sum(items))

Run python3 total.py and confirm it prints 5. Keep a Git baseline of the test files. In this scratch project, use the following opencode.json to deny tool actions during the check. This setting controls permissions. For a separate process or network boundary, use an isolated environment.

{
  "permissions": [
    { "action": "*", "resource": "*", "effect": "deny" }
  ]
}

Commit the test files with Git, then run git status --short. A clean baseline prints nothing. Leave unrelated plugins and project instructions out of this scratch project so the result is easier to interpret.

Run the first session and verify the answer

Replace PROVIDER/MODEL with the exact ID you selected. Passing the file with --file gives the model that file’s contents. The -- separates the file options from the prompt.

opencode run --standalone --agent plan \
  --model PROVIDER/MODEL --file total.py -- \
  "What does the attached Python file print? Reply with the number only."

Compare the answer with python3 total.py and compare git status --short with your baseline. If the answer is missing, verify the provider and model ID. If the answer differs, keep the actual program output as the reference. With Ollama, ollama ps immediately after the request can confirm the model loaded.

In our macOS arm64 test, OpenCode 2.4.1 discovered Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct Q4_K_M through Ollama 0.40.18. A first prompt returned READY_CHECK. A follow-up in the same session answered 5 for the attached file, matching Python. Git remained clean. The test used a custom loopback port, a 32-token output cap and temperature zero. Both processes were restricted to loopback and tool actions were denied. This verifies the first local run and file attachment, without measuring coding quality or testing hosted providers. Download the first-run results.

Continue with your own repository

  • Before permitting edits, check the OpenCode permission rules and the Git diff.
  • Put shared build checks in AGENTS.md. Inspect which config is loaded if a model or setting differs across directories.
  • To pick up a previous task, resume the exact session and verify its history.

See the CLI command reference and the model selector reference.
